band_change_evidence_test.explanation: The test fails on the tier requirement. Four independent sources were used — Live Science, ZME Science, RoboZaps and Tracxn — which satisfies the two-source part. None reaches tier 4, and only the two February 2025 reports of the Protoclone reveal reach tier 3. Clone Robotics publishes no institutional data, no responsibility report and no audited disclosure, and no independent assessment of the company exists. Critically, the two facts carrying the four floor-level subdimension scores both come from a single tier-2 source and were not independently corroborated. The band change should be treated as provisional and the score as the least secure in the study.

key_evidence: Why it matters: Clone Robotics is the thinnest entity in this cluster. It has 50 staff, $7.1 million raised, no shipped product and no published policy of any kind — and it was labelled "Established", the benchmark’s second-highest band.

Clone Robotics unveiled Protoclone in February 2025: over 1,000 artificial muscles, 500 sensors and 206 bones. The video passed 50 million views and drew reactions ranging "from disdain to outright hostility".
As of 23 July 2026 no Clone Alpha can be bought, no orderable price has ever been published, and there is no public evidence a single unit has shipped.

The company’s own pre-order page has said "Pre-orders available in 2025" since December 2024 and was still saying it, unchanged, nineteen months later. That drives the lowest Scope Clarity score in the cluster.

No adverse conduct was found — no lawsuits, no safety incidents, no labour findings. Three subdimensions score at the floor of 1, and all three rest on documented gaps between what the company said and what it delivered, not on harm.

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — SEED CORRECTION, NOT A CONDUCT DOWNGRADE. The published 60.9 is a never-assessed uniform placeholder shared byte-for-byte with nine other robotics labs. Clone Robotics has never been individually assessed. NO adverse conduct of any kind was located. Thirty-six of forty subdimensions score at the low anchor for absence of disclosure. The four scores at the floor of 1 rest on documented delivery gaps, not on harm. THIS IS THE THINNEST ENTITY IN THE STUDY: 50 employees, $7.1M raised, no shipped product, no published policy, no independent assessment. The band-change evidence test FAILS on tier. A coordinator should consider whether a pre-revenue 50-person company with no shipped product belongs in a published ranking at all, which is a scope question rather than a scoring one.
